articles.title: Adaptive Concurrency Limits in Go: Dynamically Protecting Dependencies Under Load
articles.excerpt: Most services eventually need a concurrency limit. You might start with something simple: const maxConcurrentRequests = 100 A semaphore ensures that no more than 100 requests execute simultaneously. I…
articles.body: Most services eventually need a concurrency limit. You might start with something simple: const maxConcurrentRequests = 100 A semaphore ensures that no more than 100 requests execute simultaneously. It works. Until the conditions change. Your service gets more CPU resources after scaling. A downstream database becomes slower. A new deployment changes request processing time. Traffic patterns shift throughout the day. The limit that worked yesterday might be too restrictive today. Or worse, it might be too high and allow a dependency to become overloaded. Static concurrency limits are easy to implement, but they require continuous tuning. What if a service could adjust its concurrency limit automatically based on how the dependency behaves?

articles.title: Enforcing maximum concurrent SIP calls without race conditions
articles.excerpt: By Rokas Remeika. Published 18 October 2026. To prevent concurrent workers from overcommitting a SIP trunk, capacity checks and claims must occur inside the same atomic database transaction. Reading a…
articles.body: By Rokas Remeika. Published 18 October 2026. To prevent concurrent workers from overcommitting a SIP trunk, capacity checks and claims must occur inside the same atomic database transaction. Reading a live-session count and writing a claim in separate steps allows workers to interleave and breach the limit. For scheduled calls, point-in-time checks fail because calls occupy time, not just an instant. Project capacity over a grid of five-minute slots spanning the call's estimated duration, and admit the call against the worst overlapping interval rather than the current count. Symptoms Your SIP trunk carrier rejects outbound legs outright because you exceeded your licensed channel capacity.

articles.title: This Android gaming benchmark app does something I’ve never seen before
articles.excerpt: Evolve is a new gaming benchmark that shows you where mobile GPUs are hitting a bottleneck.
articles.body: Credit: Harish Jonnalagadda / Android Authority I like benchmarks a little too much and use them on every new phone I test. Synthetic benchmarks like Geekbench and 3DMark do a good job of simulating real-world usage and gaming scenarios, and they predict a device’s performance potential reasonably well. As someone who gets over 75 phones a year, a synthetic benchmark lets me easily measure how a particular device holds up against its predecessor. There’s a new benchmark that aims to go beyond just delivering an overall score. It’s called Evolve , and it provides useful insights across five metrics, allowing you to then pinpoint which part of the GPU is handling modern workloads well, and what’s causing a potential bottleneck.

articles.body: This is a great month for planet watching, either in the evenings or mornings. During convenient evening hours, the planet of choice is Saturn , visible well up in the southern sky during mid-to-late evening hours. Telescopically, the southern side of its famous ring system is currently tilted about 6½ degrees to our line of sight. Around the middle of the night, Mars and Jupiter come into view above the east-northeast horizon and just before the break of dawn are in excellent position, soaring high in the southern sky in the vicinity of the Sickle of Leo the Lion. Watch how Mars approaches Jupiter early in the month, passes it on Nov. 16, then spends the rest of the month sailing away to the east.

articles.title: 9 nightmarish sci-fi spaceships to crawl aboard for Halloween if you dare
articles.excerpt: Grab your high-lumen flashlight and gargantuan gun to explore these vicious vessels
articles.body: Abandoned, possessed, or infested spaceships in sci-fi films, books, and video games are usually not a welcoming place to hang your helmet and kick back inside. Many are distinctly marked as DO NOT APPROACH zones and equipped with clearly articulated warning messages to keep your distance, but that doesn't ever seem to stop scavengers, space pirates, or evil industrial mega corporations from waving off these dangerous signs to board anyway. Other creaky craft are apt to contain nasty alien hitchhikers or biological hazards not exactly conducive to a pleasant star-trekking voyage. Whether these nefarious neglected craft have just reappeared from the other side of a black hole or have been lying dormant for eons on a hostile planetoid, visitors are usually infrequent.

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
